declared.title: Not Learning From Failure—the Greatest Failure of All
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « Not learning from failure the greatest failure of all » (2026-11-23); line of research named in the idea scout's notes

population: adults in 5 experiments (total N = 1,674), binary-choice questions in professional, linguistic and social domains; countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: People told they had answered wrong learned less, on a follow-up test, than people told they had answered right, although both kinds of feedback gave away the correct answer

support.sentence: However, on a follow-up test, participants learned less from failure feedback than from success feedback.

findings.text: The authors explain the gap by ego threat: a personal failure makes people tune out

support.sentence: Failure is ego threatening, which causes people to tune out.

findings.text: People learned less from their own failure than from their own success, but as much from other people's failures as from others' successes

support.sentence: Participants learned less from personal failure than from personal success, yet they learned just as much from other people's failure as from others' success.

limits: laboratory: binary-choice questions, learning tested minutes later; not failures in life
Spiller 2025 (Psychological Science commentary) argues the core task's scoring can produce this gap with equal learning; no reply found
the result on others' failures is one part of the paper, its size not given in the abstract
samples and countries not given in the abstract (full text not read)
